newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge down on profit-taking, seen up.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge down on profit-taking, seen up.

text.p: Profit-taking pushed down leading Russian shares on Friday, traders said, but forecast prices would rise on Monday as eager investors began snapping up the cheaper shares.
The Russian Trading System of 22 shares slipped by 1.82 percent to 493.34 on $75.3 million in total market volume.

UES EESR.RTS power utility ordinaries fell to $0.4356 from $0.4505, Mosenergo MSNG.RTS power utility was $1.530 after $1.574, Rostelekom RTKM.RTS telecoms company fell to $4.65 from $4.83. Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS metals was unchanged at $13.70.
Foreign investors took some profit and Russian investors jumped onto the bandwagon after a month of surging prices..
"Now everyone is scared to be late -- the market was high and now everyone decided to take profit and leave for the week-end quietly," said ING-Bank trader Oleg Galkin.
But he said there was still demand and the market was waiting for lower prices.
"There was money on the market for the whole week, just waiting for the moment to enter," he said. "Those who want to buy seem to be waiting. I think buying will start on Monday."
Trinfiko Securities Department Head Ilya Galtsov said investors' interest would be shifting from leading shares into the second-tier ones, adding second-tier oil shares rose.
"All the oil shares are in demand because production-sharing business is progressing," he said.
At the start of July Russia's upper house of parliament approved a list of deposits open to development under production-sharing deals.
Noyabrskneftegaz NZGZ.RTS oil company ordianry shares rose to $12.75 from $11.75 at Thursday's close, Nizhnevartovskneftegaz oil producer NZGS.RTS was $15.00 from $13.00.
